A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HyperMARL work. Their main texts, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable, allowing retained, relocated and revised material to be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original matrix-game experiments, VMAS and SMAX evaluations, policy-diversity measurements, gradient-variance measurements and ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds MAMuJoCo evaluations, argmax matrix-game evaluations, additional ablations and an extended-training comparison.

M1.justification: The core hypernetworks, embeddings and learning objective remain unchanged. However, v2 Section 5.2 introduces an actor-only application for MAMuJoCo, retaining a centralized, non-shared critic instead of generating both actor and critic parameters. This is a limited procedural adaptation.

E1.justification: V2 adds four MAMuJoCo control tasks: Humanoid, Walker2d, HalfCheetah and Ant, including coordination among 17 Humanoid agents. This substantially extends specialization testing into articulated-body control. The matrix games, VMAS scenarios and four SMAX maps are retained.

E2.justification: V2 Table 4 introduces evaluated comparisons with HAPPO, a sequential-update method designed for heterogeneous agents. V1 mentioned HAPPO only in related work and excluded its category from the analysis. This substantially extends the comparison framework; the existing IPPO, MAPPO and DiCo comparisons remain.

E3.justification: V2 adds systematic argmax evaluation in Table 2 while retaining sampled-action evaluation in Table 6. New protocols include MAMuJoCo training for 10 million timesteps, evaluation over 40 episodes every 25 training episodes, and a 40-million-step FuPS control on Dispersion. Existing VMAS and SMAX settings are retained.

E4.justification: V2 adds ablations removing gradient decoupling and initialization scaling, evaluates component choices on Humanoid and Dispersion, and tests whether longer training rescues MAPPO-FuPS. V1's Hyperfan-initialization ablation is removed. Capacity and embedding comparisons, together with parameter-count controls, remain.

E5.justification: V2 replaces diversity boxplots with explicit mean-and-standard-deviation reporting and overlap markers, and newly specifies five seeds for Navigation. Existing bootstrap-CI practices remain. The gradient-variance caption loses v1's identification of error bars as standard errors; v2 does not define their replacement. No increase in run counts is established.

E6.justification: V2 adds MAMuJoCo results, the full argmax game-results table, new ablation outcomes and extended-training results. For Humanoid, Table 4 reports HyperMARL at 6544.10 and HAPPO at 6501.15, with overlapping confidence intervals. V1 Table 2 survives unchanged as v2 Table 6; its matrix-game learning curves and Hyperfan-ablation results are absent.

T1.justification: Section 4.4 now derives gradients using an explicitly centralized critic and an advantage based on joint histories and actions, replacing v1's local observation/action formulation. The chain-rule factorization, specialization definition, SND definition and shared-policy 0.75-bound proof are retained; the proof moves to Appendix B.

C1.justification: V2 elevates the claim that gradient decoupling is critical for specialization into its main contributions. V1 emphasized the association with lower gradient variance and robustness to tested design choices. The central claims about adaptive hypernetworks, unchanged learning objectives and NoPS-level diversity remain.

C2.justification: V2 interprets component-removal experiments as establishing the importance of decoupling and initialization on Humanoid, and extended training as evidence of persistent FuPS underperformance. V1 suggested additional training might help FuPS and emphasized robust final performance across its tested variants. V2's 'similar findings' wording for Dispersion needs qualification: Figure 17's variant without initialization scaling still converges.

D1.justification: V2 adds Algorithm 1 pseudocode and extensive MAMuJoCo implementation information, including architectures, optimization settings, per-task defaults and HyperMARL clipping sweeps. Existing benchmark hyperparameters are largely retained and reorganized. Both versions still promise future code availability.

R1.justification: V2 adds substantive positioning against concurrent CASH, distinguishing agent conditioning and fixed task spaces from capability-conditioned zero-shot generalization. It also incorporates Kaleidoscope and gradient-conflict literature, supplies baseline-selection rationales, and brings previously excluded HAPPO into the empirical comparison framework.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method exposition and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten. Experiments are organized around two research questions, while the proof, diversity definition, scalability discussion and experimental details move into a substantially reorganized appendix structure.

P2.justification: V2 changes typography, headers and citation presentation; separates Dispersion learning curves from convergence plots; converts diversity boxplots into a table; and adds algorithm, environment, baseline and MAMuJoCo displays. Numerous retained figures are resized or relocated. Some captions introduce errors, notably Figure 15 labeling MAMuJoCo plots as SMAX.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens evidence beyond v1's relatively simple specialization tasks: MAMuJoCo and HAPPO comparisons test complex heterogeneous coordination, component-removal ablations examine the proposed mechanism, and extended FuPS training addresses a sample-efficiency alternative. Pseudocode and task-specific settings improve reproducibility. These gains outweigh reporting and caption inconsistencies and overly broad initialization wording, whose applicability differs between Figures 7 and 17.
